column1: # THE MULTI-YEAR ROWS (2026-09-29; the decline length rows added and every row regenerated from
# published sources 2026-09-30): the record's own reading of `multiYearReadings` /
# `multi_year_readings`, the statistics a year or more of a series is one observation of.
# annual autocorr           the lag-1 correlation of successive annual log changes
# variance ratio 3y, 5y     the variance of k-year log changes over k times the variance of the
#                           annual changes across the same span; 1 without serial dependence
# 3y p95 excess             the 95th percentile of the log return over every 756-session window,
#                           less the series' own mean 3-year return
# decline gap p90 y         the 90th percentile of the years between the peaks of successive
# decline length p50 y      the median peak-to-trough length in years of the regained declines of
#                           20% or more (a censored decline's trough is provisional)
# decline length max y      the longest of them
# under water 20% %         sessions more than 20% under the running peak, in percent
# Block statistics are averaged over twelve phases spread evenly across the block's own length.
# Each statistic is a row twice: against the set's equity window, and against its long window
# under the name with `long` appended.  The record's eras disagree -- CRSP's annual autocorrelation
# reads +0.03 over the century and -0.13 from 1954, its time under water 25.5% and 12.6% -- so a
# world is read against both.  The Nasdaq grades its long window alone, the IXIC+NDX splice over
# 1971-2026 (2026-10-03): its QQQ rows and its NDX rows are reported, not graded
# (`NASDAQ_REPORTED`), since both windows lie inside the one the consumer's rules were selected on.
# Graded by where the record falls among the world's single histories of the window's length: a
# one-year block resample has no multi-year structure left to read.  A row misses when the record
# falls outside the family's joint band of those histories, which a world the record is a typical
# history of clears on every row at once 90% of the time.
# records, and a test per twin re-derives them.
# nasdaq  QQQ, Yahoo Finance's adjusted closes, 1999-03-11..2026-08-20; long window IXIC+NDX,
#         the Nasdaq Composite's daily log returns through 1985-10-01 and the Nasdaq-100's after
#         (Yahoo Finance's ^IXIC and ^NDX closes; price indexes), 1971-02-08..2026-09-18, the bubble window;
#         reported, the NDX PRICE index alone, 1990-01-03..2026-09-18.
# sp500   CRSP value-weighted US market total return from Ken French's
#         F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily (202606): Mkt-RF + RF compounded into an index without
#         a leading 1.0, then its log returns; 1954-2026, and the century as the long window.
